tools.description: Return the Balance Sheet for a date range, derived from Tally's native Trial Balance: one line per reserved Balance Sheet primary group (Capital Account, Loans (Liability), Current Liabilities, Suspense A/c, Branch / Divisions, Fixed Assets, Investments, Current Assets, Misc. Expenses (ASSET)), each the signed closing balance at `to` (a debit negative), and `result.profit_and_loss`: the Profit & Loss A/c ledger's closing and the `carried` result (that closing plus every P&L ledger's closing; in a part-year window the year's earlier result sits in that ledger). The top-level `lines` is null while `carried` is not established, so a derived line is never shown as the statement. Reads the Trial Balance, the group tree, Tally's own Balance Sheet and its Profit and Loss inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket; requires one INR currency master and supported date boundaries. Each line's `amount` has `sum` (of the amounts Tally returned), `present_count` and `empty_count`. A result is established only if every ledger is classified (a ledger under a user-created primary group, or whose group chain is incomplete, is listed in `unclassified`, up to 100, with `unclassified_total`), no Stock-in-Hand ledger carries an amount, and Tally's own Balance Sheet for the window ties line for line to the derived one (`balance_sheet_gate`). Otherwise it is `not_established` with a `reason` (`unclassified_ledger_carries_an_amount`, `closing_stock_not_derivable_from_trial_balance`, `profit_and_loss_ledger_not_returned`, `tally_balance_sheet_differs`); for that reason `lines` names the lines that did not tie. On the one book measured, Tally's own Balance Sheet export left out the Difference in opening balances line its screen showed: when the export's lines do not sum to zero the result carries `tally_balance_sheet_sides` (the credit and debit totals), the first line says so, and nothing is established (`tally_balance_sheet_does_not_balance` when no other reason applies). The top-level `state` is `observed` only while `carried` is established, else `not_established` with the nested `reason`. With integrated inventory and no opening stock, Tally's own Profit and Loss `Less: Closing Stock` is used (not in Current Assets) and shown in `closing_stock`, only if that one figure ties Current Assets, this line and Cost of Sales, and the lines sum to zero (one book seen); otherwise a book with stock items refuses. A Tally line with an amount and no derived counterpart (a heading) refuses. Tally's statements name no company; the checks around the read bind them. The gate has been measured over one full year on one book and one month on another; a window spanning more than one financial year is unmeasured. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: Validate a Journal, Payment, Receipt or Contra batch and read its current verification window before writing a local import file. A proposals file with a cash withdrawal or deposit not yet answered is refused (cash_questions_open); a ledger named in a cash answer is checked against the book's groups (cash_ledger_not_cash_in_hand for a business-cash ledger outside Cash-in-Hand, cash_answer_ledger_in_suspense for a non-dont_know ledger under Suspense A/c). A proposals file whose bank_ledger is under Cash-in-Hand is refused (statement_bank_ledger_not_a_bank), because a statement belongs to a bank account; a suspense_ledger outside Suspense A/c, with a group that cannot be established, or absent from the book, builds with a typed entry in statement_ledger_warnings (suspense_ledger_outside_suspense_group, suspense_ledger_group_not_established, suspense_ledger_not_in_book). Inline vouchers carry no such checks. The result's suspense_lines counts every voucher whose narration ends in a ComplyEaze Bridge suspense tag, by tag (purpose_not_confirmed, unidentified), and lists none. Other parts of a result are built from the vouchers themselves: verification_preflight's from and to span the batch's earliest and latest voucher dates (for an amendment, also the dates its batch's earlier builds recorded; an amendment refused as not as built returns the same window), total_debit and total_credit sum the batch (so a batch of one voucher returns that voucher's date and amount), and an amendment's voucher lists and some refusals name vouchers by bridge_txn_id, which for a parse_bank_statement proposal carries the statement row's date after st-. A batch holds Journals only, or Payment, Receipt and Contra vouchers only (those three may share one): a batch mixing the two is refused as voucher_type_shapes_mixed, so build one batch of each. Every build reads each voucher type's voucher numbering from Tally after the mark, and writes a voucher only into a voucher type that reads Automatic with the sub-method Auto Retain, the screen's Retain Original Voucher No. (where Tally discards a number the voucher carries and assigns the next), or, for a Journal that carries its own voucher number, Manual with duplicate numbers prevented (where Tally keeps the number and refuses one a Journal already holds): any other reading is refused as import_voucher_numbering_not_automatic (a voucher type that does not read Automatic, Automatic (Manual Override) included) or import_voucher_numbering_not_retain (Automatic without Auto Retain), a batch holding both is refused as import_voucher_numbering_not_automatic, each such voucher type is named in refused_types with what was read, and no file is written. Under Manual voucher numbering a second voucher sent without a number was seen to take a number already used, or to be refused; with a voucher type set to Renumber Vouchers (the series reads Auto Renumber) Tally was seen to change the numbers of vouchers already in the book when a voucher with an earlier date was entered by hand, and again when one was sent by import without a number, while the import's answer reported nothing altered and no voucher's AlterID moved (one book, TallyPrime 7.1 Silver: by import on a Receipt and a Journal, by hand on a Receipt); a Receipt that carried a number was given the number of its place in date order there; a file of more than two vouchers, a file that mixes numbered and numberless vouchers, a Journal that carries a number or is dated after every other, Payment and Contra there, Gold, other releases and the same through ComplyEaze Bridge's own post are not measured. A numbering read that fails keeps its own code (a voucher type saved during it refuses it as masters_bound_premise_violated, cause masters_alter_id_above_master_mark: build again), and a book in Education mode is refused as masters_education_unqualified. The check holds for the moment of the read: a voucher type changed after the build is not caught when the file is imported by hand. The sub-method was measured on one release and edition only: on a release, an edition or a book whose series prints none, or words it differently, every Automatic voucher type is refused, and masters with kind voucher_types shows what a book prints (series_numbering.sub_method). Import a bank statement in whole-day batches: cut a batch only between days, at most 50 vouchers (the most one batch post takes), since same-day rows with one type, ledgers and amounts pass the post's check together in one batch, while one that an earlier batch posted refuses the whole later batch as import_preexisting_identity; a proposals file is whole days already (from and to are days), and a day with more than 50 rows does not fit one batch, an open limit: ask the user. With posting on, a saved batch of up to 50 posts after one approval, so same-day twins post together in one batch or through a hand import of the built file. Every named ledger's bill-wise flag (ISBILLWISEON) comes from the ledger list this build already reads, once before the mark and again at the catalogue repeat, so no extra request is made. A ledger list whose flag is missing, repeated or, after trimming, not exactly Yes or No fails as ledger_export_invalid, with a cause beginning ledger_catalogue_bill_wise_flag_, and a list that changed between the two reads, a flag included, is refused as import_catalogue_changed. An entry on a bill-wise ledger carries no bill allocation, so it is expected to land On Account in Tally, on any side of any voucher type (measured for one party leg on one book; Tally decides by the ledger, not the voucher type, but other legs and types are not measured). Each such ledger is a party, and a batch naming one is refused as bill_wise_party_unapproved, listing for each party in refused_parties its row_count, debit_total, credit_total, its rows with date and amount (rows_omitted counts those not listed; raise BRIDGE_AGENT_MAX_BYTES to list them all) and a party_digest. Ask the person, one party per question, whether that party's entries may post On Account, then build again with on_account_approvals, a list of {party_digest} for each party they said yes to (the digest alone says which party; a ledger copied beside it is not read, so a masked name does no harm). The digest ties an approval to this exact batch, company and endpoint, and changing any row changes every party's digest; it does NOT prove that a person said yes, so never approve on the person's behalf. The native approval dialog marks each approved party On Account, from the build's record: before its name on each of its entries for one voucher, and on its totals line for a batch (not on a batch's per-voucher lines); a hand import of the file is not checked at all. A ledger switched to bill-wise after the build, and not approved, is refused at post as import_bill_wise_changed: build again and ask the person about it. A saved batch built before this check refuses to post as import_batch_predates_bill_wise_record; first check in Tally whether its file was already imported by hand, then build it again. Every build creates a new batch identity, even for reused transaction labels, except an amendment (amends_batch_id, whose description says what it compares and when it is refused); an amendment also needs each voucher's ALTERID to equal the one ComplyEaze Bridge recorded when it first verified a build the book matches, so it needs that verification and refuses a voucher altered since (voucher_altered_since_verified, voucher_never_verified). Verifying now records this voucher exactly as it stands in Tally, including any changes made since ComplyEaze Bridge built it. Check the voucher in Tally first; if someone has edited it, correct it there instead of amending. The check runs when the amendment is built, not when it is imported: the import is done by hand in Tally, and an edit made there in between is overwritten without warning, so import promptly. Import and verify each amendment before building the next one for the same voucher: two amendments built from the same state overwrite each other, and the later import wins. If any import outcome is uncertain, preserve the original batch and saved file, then reconcile with verify_import without writing; an amendment is not recovery, and is refused for a voucher not found in the book. Otherwise do not re-import or rebuild the same business event, including a Journal; a repeat observation does not qualify recovery after an unknown outcome. Later changes may exceed read limits. Other voucher types are unqualified. A batch that is not an amendment and holds a row that another batch of this company already sent to Tally, or that a readback found posted, is refused here as import_txn_already_posted and no file is written: verify_import the batch that blocking_batch_id names, and build again without the row. A batch you imported by hand blocks nothing until verify_import records the whole batch posted (an incomplete or divergent readback does not count), so check that before rebuilding any of its rows. This check is a point in time: a batch sent after this file was built is not seen by it, so import this file promptly and verify it. A build from a version 2 parse_bank_statement proposals file also records that statement's skipped rows and its Contras, and every successful build returns a transfers section for the company: state (computed, or not_established when the view could not be computed or the section was cut to fit; a written build that fits only without even that note is answered without the section and the answer is marked truncated), skips_paired, skips_open, open (each skipped row that is neither paired with a verified Contra of the other account nor retired, by bridge_txn_id and date only, never an amount, reference or ledger, with its state: not_found, other_side_unverified or held_elsewhere (batch_id names the batch to verify), posted_against_skip (batch_id names a batch found posted that posts the row although a statement skipped it and no build in its lineage that was sent or found posted recorded its withdrawal after the newest record of the skip: the other account's Contra may carry the transfer too, no step inside ComplyEaze Bridge removes a posted voucher, and the row leaves the list only when a build in that batch's lineage naming it in withdraw_skips is found posted after the newest record of the skip, which cannot happen for a batch ComplyEaze Bridge posted itself), ambiguous or reversed_same_day (batch_id, where there is one, names a batch holding a Contra that could carry the row, one row for each such batch: ComplyEaze Bridge does not choose), matched_unconfirmed (batch_id names the batch whose verified Contra matches the row by day and amount, while the statement records of the two accounts do not both cover that day: keep the skip), reference_differs (batch_id names a batch holding a Contra of the same day and amount whose reference differs from the row's, one row for each such batch: ComplyEaze Bridge cannot tell whether it is the row's other side), or not_established; and each Contra booked from two statements as double_booked, with the other batch), open_omitted (raise BRIDGE_AGENT_MAX_BYTES to list every open row), retired (skips named in withdraw_skips, once every batch found posted that holds the row has a build in its lineage that recorded the withdrawal, sent or found posted after the newest record of the skip), and next_steps with what to do for each state present. Do not enter a listed transfer in Tally by hand: a later post of the other statement would book it twice. not_established means that the other account's statement for that date is not built and verified through ComplyEaze Bridge, that a Contra or statement row on that bank on that date is one the statement records cannot see or use (built from inline vouchers or by a release before them), or that the check could not run; it never means nothing is missing. A statement of which every row is skipped writes no import file: it returns state skips_recorded, a record_id and the same section. Three more refusals come before anything is written, each with a next_step: skip_row_already_posted (this build skips a row that is already a voucher of a batch of the company sent to Tally or found posted, or of the batch it amends; blocking_batch_id names it), skip_row_paired_elsewhere (this build posts a row that a statement of the company skipped as carried by the other account's Contra, in a batch sent to Tally or found posted or in a statement of only skipped rows; skipped_rows lists them), and transfer_double_booked (a Contra of this build carries a transfer that another statement already booked as a Contra with an equal reference; other_batch_id names that batch). withdraw_skips is an optional list of such skipped rows to post anyway: name a row only when the person confirms the other account's statement does not carry it; each must be a skip held for the company (in a batch, whether or not it was sent, or in a statement of only skipped rows) and a voucher of this build, or the build is refused as withdraw_skip_invalid. A withdrawal is refused while exactly one verified Contra matches the row and nothing else claims that Contra. Where more than one verified Contra matches, the match is also claimed by another row or booked twice, the amount reverses the same day and the match is by date, or the only match carries a different reference and is verified, ComplyEaze Bridge cannot tell which entry the row belongs to: the withdrawal is then the person's explicit choice, and the batch of every matching Contra is listed on the row in the transfers section. While the only match is not yet verified, the withdrawal is refused and the step says to verify that entry first. So is one with any match in a batch not yet verified, whatever the row's state: a person can confirm only what Tally holds. Such a withdrawal is refused as withdraw_skip_paired, naming each such batch with the row's state there (paired, matched_unconfirmed or other_side_unverified). A Contra matches a row by an equal reference, or by the same date and amount where one of the two carries no reference. One of the same day and amount whose reference differs from the row's is a match only for a row that nothing else matches. One dated another day, or with a third leg, does not match, so verify every batch of the other account's statement before naming a row. When ComplyEaze Bridge cannot read its own record of skipped rows and Contras, a build that carries a statement's facts, posts a statement row or names withdraw_skips is refused as transfer_view_not_established, and any other build goes on with transfers.state not_established. This never dispatches import XML to Tally. Reads Tally to check the vouchers, then writes the prepared import file and a ledger record to ComplyEaze Bridge's local folder on this computer (for a statement of only skipped rows, no import file: one record of those rows); writes nothing to Tally.

amends_batch_id.description: Correct vouchers of a batch ComplyEaze Bridge built on this computer, in place. Name that batch (or an earlier amendment of it); every bridge_txn_id must be one that batch or one of its amendments built, with the same voucher_type, voucher_number and reference (a changed, added or removed reference is refused, import_amend_voucher_reference_changed: the import could not be confirmed; change it in Tally after the amendment is imported and verified). The file reuses that batch's REMOTEIDs, so a file import alters the vouchers instead of duplicating them. Refused if any build of that batch was posted natively, and refused unless each named voucher is still in the book as a build of that batch wrote it in the fields compared (date, a bank voucher's effective date when Tally returns one, type, number when set, entries' ledger, amount and side, narration) — checked during this build only, not at import. A reference, bill-wise or cost-centre allocations and the party ledger are not compared, and allocations made in Tally are expected to be lost when the file is imported (not measured directly).

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

on_account_approvals.description: One entry per bill-wise party the person agreed may receive this batch's entries On Account, copied from a bill_wise_party_unapproved refusal of the same batch: its party_digest, which alone says which party is approved (ledger may be copied beside it, and is not read: with party names masked it is a masked name). Leave it out on the first build. A digest that is not one of this batch's parties' digests, or one given twice, is refused as on_account_approval_invalid (cause digest_differs, duplicate or malformed): nothing is accepted and dropped. The digest ties an approval to this exact batch, company, endpoint and ledger; it does not prove that a person said yes.

proposals_id.description: Build from a proposals file parse_bank_statement wrote, instead of `vouchers`. Its vouchers are admitted exactly as inline ones would be. Requires proposals_sha256.

proposals_sha256.description: The sha256 parse_bank_statement returned for that proposals file; the build is refused if the file no longer has it.

vouchers.description: Exactly one of vouchers or proposals_id. At most 100 distinct ledger names across the batch; repeated ledgers do not reduce the 1000-voucher limit.

ledger.description: The ledger's exact live name. It may end in one CR LF only when the live ledger's stored name does, as validate_masters reports it in exact_live_spelling; no other control character is accepted. A name that folds equal to another live ledger's name or to one of its aliases (case, spacing, dashes, slashes or quotes, a trailing line break) is refused as ledger_has_folded_twin; a ledger in the refusal only because of an alias carries through_alias.

narration.description: Nonempty text without control characters. The reserved [BRIDGE: marker is forbidden in every ASCII case, including XML entity-encoded spellings.

reference.description: Nonempty text without control characters. The reserved [BRIDGE: marker is forbidden in every ASCII case, including XML entity-encoded spellings.

voucher_type.description: Journal takes any balanced set of entries and may carry voucher_number and reference. Payment, Receipt and Contra take two or more entries (for more than two, one three-entry Receipt built by ComplyEaze Bridge has been imported over the gateway and verified; no multi-entry Payment or Contra has been, and none of the three, including that Receipt, through Tally's Import menu), at least one debit and one credit and no ledger on both sides, and neither of those fields, and are refused unless every money-side entry names a ledger whose live group ancestry reaches Bank Accounts or Cash-in-Hand: every credit on a Payment, every debit on a Receipt, every leg on a Contra. Every remaining leg of a Payment or Receipt must be established as holding no money: any money group there means the voucher is really a Contra, and a ledger whose group ancestry cannot be resolved is refused as well. These rules span fields and live masters, so the server enforces them after admission rather than here.

withdraw_skips.description: Statement rows (the bridge_txn_id of a parse_bank_statement proposal, st- followed by the row's date and hash) that a statement of this company skipped as carried by the other account's Contra, and that this build posts anyway as a voucher of any type. A build that posts a row such a skip names is refused as skip_row_paired_elsewhere unless this names it, because posting it books its own bank and, if the other account's Contra exists, books the transfer twice. The refusal reads only a skip held by a statement of only skipped rows or by a batch sent to Tally or found posted, not one in a batch that has only been built. Name a row only when the person confirms the other account's statement does not carry it; never on their behalf. Each row must be a skip ComplyEaze Bridge holds for this company (in a batch, whether or not it was sent, or in a statement of only skipped rows) and a voucher of this build, or the build is refused as withdraw_skip_invalid. A withdrawal is refused while exactly one verified Contra matches the row and nothing else claims that Contra. Where more than one verified Contra matches, the match is also claimed by another row or booked twice, the amount reverses the same day and the match is by date, or the only match carries a different reference and is verified, ComplyEaze Bridge cannot tell which entry the row belongs to: the withdrawal is then the person's explicit choice, and the batch of every matching Contra is listed on the row in the transfers section. While the only match is not yet verified, the withdrawal is refused and the step says to verify that entry first. So is one with any match in a batch not yet verified, whatever the row's state: a person can confirm only what Tally holds. Such a withdrawal is refused as withdraw_skip_paired. The batch records the names. A withdrawn skip is held by the new batch until it is found posted, and is retired once every batch found posted that holds the row has a build in its lineage that recorded the withdrawal, sent or found posted and built after the newest record of the skip (a later build of the skipping statement records it again); otherwise it stays open as posted_against_skip.

tools.description: Return Tally's own Cash Flow for whole months: its month-wise movement of the cash and bank ledgers, not a cash flow statement under AS 3. The months are returned only after the net total of the whole period has been compared with the trial balance, over the ledgers this check counts as cash and bank (those under Cash-in-Hand and Bank Accounts, a group inside them included; a ledger under a group a user made inside one was not measured), and found equal; otherwise the result is not_established and no month is shown (cash_flow_differs_from_trial_balance; cash_flow_money_group_unmeasured when a Bank OD A/c or Bank OCC A/c ledger has movement; cash_flow_nothing_to_compare when neither the cash and bank ledgers nor Tally's Cash Flow carry an amount for the period). Each month's `closing` is Tally's closing column for it, not checked month by month, and Tally's debit and credit columns are not returned. A month Tally printed with no amount is returned with an empty closing, which is not zero and does not say the month had no entries. A negative amount is a debit: cash and bank grew. The result's unmeasured_in_this_answer names any credit amount, positive closing or window from March into April it contains (a credit amount was seen tied to the trial balance in live runs on one synthetic book (two windows, one of them with a positive closing), and a window from March into April was not run; no month was compared with Tally's own Cash Flow screen: compare such months with it); two zero nets are not a tie (cash_flow_nothing_to_compare). The window must be whole months, at most twelve, and not start before the book (cash_flow_window_not_month_start, cash_flow_window_not_month_end, cash_flow_window_too_many_months, trial_balance_before_books). A book with several currency masters and Education mode are refused. The report's cost on a large book with cash activity is not known (one year of empty months on a large book answered at once): ask for one month first, and if a call times out do not repeat it. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: Return three settings Tally's company record holds today for one company: cost centres, GST and batch-wise stock (each yes, no or not_reported), and the company's currency symbol. They say nothing about what the books contain or what the settings were during a year: a cost-centre allocation can be stored while the setting reads No. Each of the three settings has been compared with Tally's own F11 screen, on three synthetic books and not on this company; a setting changed inside a sitting has not been measured. Each setting says what it rests on. The currency is the symbol Tally holds (for example the rupee sign), not an ISO code, and it does not say whether foreign currencies are used. A setting Tally did not send is not_reported, never no. Tally's other feature flags are fetched in the same request and are not returned. Nothing this tool returns changes what another tool reads or refuses. Take company_guid from list_companies. This reads the company record and the book extent twice and returns no ledger, voucher, amount or narration. A company in Education mode is refused. Never present a setting as a fact about the books or about a past period. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: Everything the assistant reads from Tally through ComplyEaze Bridge in this chat, amounts included, is sent to the AI provider; redaction can only shorten party and ledger names, bank account numbers and ledger address lines, or drop narrations, and does not hide amounts, company names, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC, MSME or Udyam registration numbers, contact details or references, or the last four digits of a bank statement's account number (account_last4); under mask_parties a name written inside a narration or reference stays as it is. Never tell the user that no data has left their computer. Shows the receipts ComplyEaze Bridge keeps of its own tool calls, read from its local log file on this computer: tool, time, company, counts and fingerprints, no figures or book content (bounded to the most recent receipts). It does not show what the AI provider received. Use it when the user asks what ComplyEaze Bridge has done, or to show a reviewer which calls ran, on which company and when. Reading the log changes nothing in it; this call's own receipt lines are added after the read, like every call's. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

limit.description: How many of the most recent receipt lines to return (each completed call writes two): default 20, at most 256 (or the configured row limit, BRIDGE_AGENT_MAX_ROWS, if lower, which can cap the default too), and fewer past a size bound; `omitted_for_size` counts those cut for the reply.

tools.description: Read-only: the GST the books record, totalled per counter ledger, for a date window; not a return figure. It does not decide input tax credit eligibility, blocked credit, what was availed, input versus output, or which row of any return a ledger belongs in, and matches nothing against any portal. It reads what purchase_register and sales_register read (the ledger masters twice, the full voucher window, the same drift checks and refusals) and, for every voucher with an entry on a ledger under Duties & Taxes whose master carries a recognised GST duty head, takes that tax per head and attributes it to the voucher's one ledger under Purchase Accounts, Direct Expenses, Indirect Expenses or Fixed Assets, only when the voucher is a Purchase, Debit Note, Journal or Payment with a ledger under Sundry Creditors on it, has exactly one such counter ledger (a round-off ledger under Indirect Expenses counts as one), and nothing besides but the party, cash, bank and TDS or TCS ledgers: a duty head does not say input or output, so a sale, a credit note or a tax payment with no supplier on it is never attributed. `counter_ledgers` lists each such ledger with its `ledger_guid` (Tally's GUID of the ledger, which trial_balance returns as the ledger's `guid`; its movement there covers every voucher on it, set-aside ones included, so it is never a base for this tax), its predefined `group`, its `parent` (masked like a ledger name when it is a group the book named), `vouchers`, `debit_side_tax` (negative, as the books state it) and `credit_side_tax` (positive: tax booked back, which can be a reversal or output tax on an asset or goods returned or sold to a supplier; the tool does not tell them apart), per head (cgst, igst, state_tax, sgst_utgst, ut_tax, cess; state_tax and sgst_utgst are both state-side and kept apart), never netted. Every other voucher with GST is set aside in `set_aside` under the first reason that applies, with its count, its own tax totals and at most 100 vouchers listed: class_not_admitted (any class but Purchase, Debit Note, Journal and Payment: sales, credit notes, memoranda), head_conflict, unrecognised_head, head_absent (a Duties & Taxes ledger that may be GST has no head), duty_ledger_without_gst_type (a Duties & Taxes ledger typed neither GST nor TDS or TCS, such as Others, which may be a GST ledger left untyped), unresolved_group (a ledger whose group does not resolve, which may be a GST ledger), sign_and_flag_disagree, entries_do_not_balance (a ledger sits where this read does not look, such as an item invoice of a shape not measured whose purchase ledger is in an inventory allocation), sales_ledger_present (sales and credit notes), gst_on_both_sides (reverse-charge and set-off journals), other_ledgers_present (a ledger under any other group, such as Current Assets or Stock-in-Hand), no_creditor_party (no ledger under Sundry Creditors, such as a GST challan payment), no_counter_ledger and several_counter_ledgers. Nothing is apportioned. Cancelled, optional and post-dated vouchers are counted, not totalled (`vouchers_cancelled_optional_or_post_dated`); `vouchers_without_gst_entry` counts the vouchers with no Duties & Taxes entry of any kind but TDS or TCS, and `vouchers_observed` every voucher of the window. A window that is not complete is refused (gst_by_ledger_window_partial). Ledger names are masked like vouchers masks them. Measured on one synthetic book of TallyPrime 7.2 Silver: fourteen vouchers typed on Tally's screen, read one day at a time and, by the build before Direct Expenses and Fixed Assets were admitted, as one month of 64 vouchers that the window read in two parts (purchases on Indirect Expenses, Direct Expenses and Fixed Assets ledgers and on two expense ledgers at once, two item invoices whose purchase ledger was among their entries, one with freight, journals with input IGST, with a TDS ledger typed Others, a set-off and a reversal with no supplier, a debit note, two tax payments, one also paying interest, and a credit note with output tax). A registered book was read once, by an earlier build: none of December's six vouchers was set aside, and a supplier invoice entered twice was totalled twice, so a duplicate is not detected. Not measured: vouchers created by import, Gold and other releases, a registered book on this build, other item-invoice shapes, more than 64 vouchers in a window. A year on a large book may be refused as too large by the window read: use shorter windows. tools.description: Return a company's ledger masters, each with its opening balance as of the start of the books (`opening_balance`, `opening_balance_as_of`), on a freshly observed supported product and mode. fields=basic (the default) or fields=compliance, which adds paired party-master observations (GSTIN, PAN, MSME, bank, contact and address), each ledger's group `ancestry` and its `gst_duty_head`. GSTIN (compliance): `party_gstin` is the GSTIN in force on `party_gstin_as_of` (the optional `as_of`, YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD such as 20260331, else this computer's date; without fields=compliance, `as_of` is refused as ledger_masters_as_of_requires_compliance), taken from the ledger's dated registration history, or from the flat GSTIN field only when that history is empty or not returned (an empty flat field names no GSTIN). `party_gstin_status`: in_force, flat_field, no_gstin_in_force (a history with no GSTIN in force on that date; `party_gstin_registration_type` says whether that entry is registered), not_reported, or history_unreadable, which fails closed (an undated, misdated, malformed, repeated or contradictory history: party_gstin is null and the flat field unused). `party_gstin_flat` is always the flat field as read; `gstin_sources_disagree` is true when it names a GSTIN the in-force entry does not: both are reported, neither is chosen. For another date, such as a transaction's, pass it as `as_of` or read the dated `compliance.gst_registrations`. Mailing details (compliance, only with `include_mailing_details`, which is not read otherwise): `compliance.mailing_details` carries the dated mailing details: `observation` is `entries` (each with `applicable_from`, `address_lines`, `pin_code`, `state`, `country`, `mailing_name` (present only when Tally sent one) and `other_content_skipped`, true when the entry held content that was not read, so its address lines may be incomplete; an empty list means the ledger has none; entries come oldest first, so for a date use the entry in force on it, the latest on or before it, not the first), `not_observed` or `unreadable` (a `defect`). Without the argument no request names the mailing details and no row has the key. The flat `address`, `pin_code`, `gst_pin_code` and `state` fields are Tally's older elements: TallyPrime 7.1 returned them empty or absent for a party that held an address in the one synthetic book measured, so read the address from `mailing_details`; other books may fill the flat fields. `mask_parties` masks `mailing_name`, every address line and the flat `address` like a party name (it shortens each line to its first two and last two characters, so a house number or a town at either end of a line can stay readable); the mailing entry's PIN code, state and country are not masked, so they reach the assistant's provider under every redaction mode (the flat `pin_code`, `gst_pin_code` and `state` already go on every compliance read, unchanged); for a party that is an individual, such as a proprietor, the flat PIN code and state sent on every compliance read, and the mailing entry's PIN code, state and country when asked for, can point to the locality of a home address. The read is admitted at 5,000 bytes a ledger instead of 3,750, above the largest row measured, not a bound. It is refused with `include_gst_details`, as the request naming both has not been captured. Duty head (compliance): `gst_duty_head` is `recognized` (`head`: cgst, igst, state_tax, sgst_utgst, ut_tax or cess; `raw`: the spelling Tally returned), `unrecognized` (raw kept), `not_tax_ledger`, `contradictory` or `absent`. `state_tax` (raw `State Tax`) and `sgst_utgst` (raw `SGST/UTGST`) are two spellings Tally has returned for a state-side head, kept apart: to sum state tax, include both. Ancestry (compliance): `chain` (nearest group first, each hop's `name` and `reserved_name`), `complete` (true only if resolved to the reserved account root) and `gap` (null when complete, else why it stopped: no_parent, group_absent, group_name_repeated, reserved_name_missing, cycle or exhausted). An incomplete chain is never padded or guessed: `chain` is exactly what was resolved, so check `complete` before treating it as exhaustive. A `reserved_name` starting with U+FFFD `#4;` is a Tally reserved value (written ``); `U+FFFD#4; Primary` is the account root, not a group a user named Primary. A ledger's `parent` that is Tally's reserved root (the Profit & Loss A/c ledger) is written ` Primary`, the text Tally sends; it is not a group name for the `group` filter. Group filter: `group` filters by group name. `group_scope` "immediate" (the default) matches only the ledger's own parent and does NOT include ledgers under sub-groups of `group`; "ancestry" matches anywhere in the resolved chain, the whole subtree (a ledger under `Bank OD A/c` matches `Loans (Liability)`), with either fields value, and a gap in a chain never counts as a match. A `group` filter reads the group collection (one more paired read with fields=basic) and returns `group_filter`: `excluded_subgroup_ledgers` (`count` left out for sitting under a sub-group of `group`, always 0 under ancestry scope, with `group_count` and up to 20 of those sub-groups in `groups`) and `unresolved_ancestry_ledgers` (ledgers not returned whose chain stops short of `group`, so whether they belong under it is unknown; counted over the whole book). GST details (compliance, opt-in): `include_gst_details` (a boolean, default false; with any other fields it is refused as ledger_masters_gst_details_requires_compliance) adds `compliance.gst_details` to each ledger: `observation` is `not_observed` (Tally returned no such list), `entries` (each dated entry with `applicable_from`, `taxability`, `source`, `ineligible_itc` and `states`; each state row has `state_name`, `slab_rates_present` and `rates` with `duty_head`, `valuation_type` and a `rate` whose `kind` is `absent`, `empty`, `zero` or `value` with `raw` as sent and `decimal`; `other_content_skipped` says content was not read) or `unreadable` (a `defect` for this ledger only). `absent`, `empty`, `zero` and `value` mean different things and are never merged. These are Tally's ledger-level details as sent: HSN/SAC and type of supply are not returned because no capture shows them, the place of supply is in the registration history, and slab rates are only flagged. `ineligible_itc` is `GSTINELIGIBLEITC` as sent (true Yes, false No, null absent): an ineligibility flag measured on one Purchase Accounts ledger only (PARTIAL), so never read true as eligible; a Yes elsewhere says nothing either way (see the result's `limitations`). The read is admitted at 8,000 bytes a ledger instead of 3,750, a margin over the one capture, not a measured ratio (the result's `limitations` has its sizes); a large book may be read in more parts or refused as too large. Large books (compliance): when the master-alteration mark (an upper bound on the ledgers, since every master raises it) puts the estimated response over budget, the ledgers are counted first, then read whole or, if the count does not fit, in parts by parent group; every counted ledger must come back exactly once, or the whole call is refused. Above a mark of 22,857 the count runs in AlterID-span slices of at most 4,000, one GUID-only request each; above 400,000 the call is refused before any ledger read (cause `ledger_catalogue_too_large`, with `size`), even for a company with fewer ledgers. Each refusal names its `cause`: `parent_over_budget`, `parent_partition_too_many_parts`, `parent_complement_over_budget`, `ledger_without_parent`, `parent_name_unsupported` (with `unsupported_parent_ledgers`), `parent_partition_duplicate_ledger_identity`, the `parent_part_*` coverage causes, `parent_part_response_too_large`, `ledger_span_slice_over_bound`, `ledger_span_duplicate_identity`, `ledger_span_census_empty`, `ledger_span_slice_malformed`, `ledger_span_identity_mismatch`, `ledger_span_slice_response_too_large` or `ledger_count_catalogue_too_large`. A size refusal refuses again on retry; fields=basic still reads the book. For `ledger_count_differs` (two counts, or a count and the ledgers read, disagree) or `ledger_count_company_differs` (Tally's own ledger count exceeds the census's), retry once while the book is quiet; for `ledger_count_company_invalid` (that count's answer was damaged) or `ledger_count_company_response_too_large`, retry once, then use fields=basic. A counted read reports `ledger_count_cross_check.status`: `matched`, `company_count_lower`, or `unavailable` (no count in Tally's answer, so no check ran). Currencies (compliance): a book with several Currency masters is read through the base Tally identifies: only plain base-currency ledgers are returned (`ledgers_scope` base_currency_ledgers_only); ledgers kept in another currency (`foreign_currency_ledgers_excluded`) and base-currency ledgers whose balances Tally shows in another currency (`base_currency_ledgers_mixed_excluded`) are named, never read. Paging: offset 0 always reads Tally afresh and holds the read; later pages are served from it while the book extent, ALTMSTID and ALTVCHID included, is unchanged, and each result reports `snapshot`. Pass the first page's `snapshot_id` on later pages to be refused as `listing_snapshot_changed` (cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`) rather than continue from a different read. With fields=compliance, repeat the first page's `as_of`: a snapshot serves only pages read as of the same date, so a later page without it (or across midnight) reads afresh, or is refused if it names the snapshot; the same holds for `include_gst_details`: a later page called without `include_gst_details` reads afresh and returns rows without `gst_details` (`snapshot.reused` false), and only a call that names snapshot_id is refused. A change that moves neither mark is not seen, so a later page can be up to 10 minutes old; every screen action measured so far moved one (a regroup, an opening change, a ledger create or delete, a voucher delete, a cancel, a save with no change; protocol reference section 11c.5, one run each). For what parties owe or are owed now, by their open bills, use outstandings instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: List a company's masters of one kind: voucher types with the numbering value Tally reports at the type level (see below: it is not their numbering method), active and optional flags and `series_numbering` (the numbering method, under Automatic its sub-method, and the duplicate setting of the type's series), godowns, units (with decimal places and whether simple), stock groups, stock items (with their own dated HSN and GST lists), cost centres (with their category), cost categories (with three allocation flags), or account groups (`groups`). Each row of another kind carries `name`, `guid`, `master_id`, `alter_id` and `parent` (null where it does not apply or is absent; a parent that is Tally's reserved root is written ` Primary`, the text Tally sends, here and in `stock_summary`, `ledger_masters`, `ledger_movement`, `gst_by_ledger` and `trial_balance`; a group a user named Primary is written plain); a `groups` row carries `name`, `parent` and `reserved_name` only. Voucher types also carry `active`, `optional` (true, false or null when Tally did not say) and `numbering_method` (`automatic`, `manual`, `default`, `{"unrecognised": <raw text>}` for any other value Tally reports, or null when absent) and `series_numbering` (`{"observation":"observed","method":"automatic"|"manual"|"automatic_manual_override"|{"unrecognised": <raw text>},"duplicates":"prevented"|"not_prevented"}`, with `"sub_method":"auto_retain"|"auto_renumber"|"absent"|{"unrecognised": <raw text>}` under `automatic` and under no other method, `{"observation":"series_count","count":n}` when a type has no series or several, and nothing is read from it, or `{"observation":"field_invalid","code":...}`), read from a second paired read of the voucher-type export and joined to each row by GUID with the name as a second equality, so a type on one side only, or a GUID and name that disagree between the two reads, refuses the whole read (`masters_numbering_names_differ` for a type in one read only, `masters_numbering_identity_differs` for a GUID and name that disagree), as do `masters_numbering_collection_changed` (the numbering read changed between its two reads) and `masters_bound_premise_violated` (the numbering answer's row count or size), and a moved book is reported as `masters_extent_changed` in place of a join or premise refusal; units carry `decimal_places` and `simple`; cost centres carry `category` (always present: a centre without one is refused), cost categories `allocates_revenue`, `allocates_non_revenue` and `affects_stock`; stock items carry `hsn` and `gst` (see below); cost centres and categories are returned whether or not the company's Cost Centres setting is on (a book with the setting off was read with its centres, and a book with it on with its own), an empty cost-centre list does not say whether the feature is off or none is defined, and an empty cost-category list is refused (`masters_cost_categories_empty`, on the expectation that the predefined Primary Cost Category always exists), and how a voucher was allocated to a cost centre is not returned by this tool: the voucher reads carry it on each ledger entry (`cost_centre_allocations`). A stock item row carries `hsn` and `gst`, each the item's own dated list as Tally sent it: an `observation` of `entries` (sorted by `applicable_from`, each entry as sent; an HSN entry has `applicable_from`, `hsn_code` as text exactly as sent (never trimmed or cut), `description`, `source` and `other_content_skipped`; a GST entry has `applicable_from`, `taxability`, `source`, `ineligible_itc` (Tally's `GSTINELIGIBLEITC` as sent: true for Yes, false for No, null when the element was absent, never filled in; on one item it was Yes on the entry whose screen row read `Eligible for Input Tax Credit: No` and absent on the entry whose screen row read Yes, which fits an ineligibility flag; PARTIAL, one book, two rows, screen against wire; what an absent element means for the tax is not known, so do not read null as eligible or as ineligible, and do not read true as eligible; on an entry whose source is `As per Company/Stock Group` (the entry Tally adds itself on a first save; a person can also choose that source) a flag Tally sent is withheld: `ineligible_itc` is null and `ineligible_itc_withheld` is `tally_default_entry`, because the Yes seen on such an entry was never compared with the screen (both screen readings are of rows a person edited or keyed, and a row's origin and its flag cannot be told apart on one item); a flag Tally did not send stays null with no marker, and an entry with any other source is sent as it is), state rows and `other_content_skipped`, and a rate is `absent`, `empty`, `zero` or a `value` with its `raw` text and `decimal`, never merged), `unreadable` with its `defect` (an undated entry, an invalid date, a repeated field, two different entries on one date, a rate that is not a plain decimal, a credit flag other than Yes or No, a repeated state or duty-head row, or content only of a kind not modelled, such as text, a reference or CDATA directly in the list; that list of that item only, the read and the row stand) or `not_observed` (the row had no such list). Nothing chooses the code or the rate for a date. An empty list (`entries` with no entry) or `not_observed` is NOT a statement that the item has no HSN code or no GST rate: what its stock group or the company holds is not read. One thing was measured, on one book: after a code was keyed on a stock group, the group's four other items still carried empty lists; not measured: a GST rate on a group or on the company, an HSN code on the company, and whether an item that defers to a coded group inherits its code. ComplyEaze Bridge does not read that setting, so every stock item row carries `inherited_from_group_or_company: not_read`. Tally adds an entry of its own to an item when it is first saved (source `As per Company/Stock Group`, no code and no rate, dated the book's first day: 1 April 2025 on the one book measured, no other book's date measured, so recognise it by its source); it says the item defers to its group or the company. `state_name` and `valuation_type` carry the reserved-character marker (U+FFFD `#4;`) where Tally sends `Any` and `Not Applicable`. A Tally ERROR or LINEERROR anywhere in a list, markup inside a value, or a list cut off refuses the whole read. Measured on one synthetic book of TallyPrime 7.1 Silver (PARTIAL): a state row other than `Any`, slab rates, another release, a larger book and a zero-row stock-item answer are not measured. One kind per call, read inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket: the extent before and after must be equal and each collection is read twice and compared, so a book that changed during the read is refused. Whole reads only. Godowns, units, stock groups, stock items, cost centres and cost categories are read only when the book's master-alteration mark times an assumed worst-case row for that kind fits 16 MB (the mark counts the masters of every kind, so a book with few of this kind can be refused), and otherwise refuse before any request with `masters_too_large` and `size` (`master_alter_id`, `estimated_bytes`, `limit_bytes`, `limit_master_alter_id`); that admits marks up to 1,152 for godowns, 1,168 for units, 1,160 for stock groups, 489 for stock items (the item row is allowed for several dated entries: it is refused past 16,344 UTF-16 units, about seven further GST entries of the measured size, whatever its state rows; a limit of 489 refuses, by arithmetic, both client books measured, not tried on them), 1,037 for cost centres and 1,264 for cost categories. Retrying refuses again. The refusal's `size` carries `limit_master_alter_id`, the largest mark this kind is read at. Both stock-heavy client books measured, with marks of about 100,000 and 300,000, refuse godowns, units and stock groups, and by the same arithmetic stock items (cost centres, cost categories and stock items were not tried on them); how common such marks are across live books is unmeasured. `voucher_types` and `groups` have no size check before the read (voucher types keep the policy of ComplyEaze Bridge's other voucher-type read, and their second, numbering read is likewise sent with no size check). After a read of any kind other than `groups`, each row's length is checked against the assumed worst-case row (`masters_row_exceeds_bound`), and the row count, the rows' AlterIDs (at or under the mark, none repeated) and the response size (each collection is read twice, and the size check runs after both reads) are checked against the mark and the admitted size; a breach of those three refuses the whole read as `masters_bound_premise_violated` and returns no partial list, unless the closing extent shows the book moved, which is reported instead (`masters_extent_changed`). A response ComplyEaze Bridge cannot read refuses at once with a `masters_*` cause, and a `voucher_types` answer with no rows refuses as `masters_voucher_types_empty`, because every company has predefined voucher types. Not returned: alias names, counts and hints (no company NUM* fields), stock-item quantities, rates and values (use stock_summary), ledgers (use ledger_masters), and any write. The row shape was captured from one synthetic book on one licensed TallyPrime 7.1 (cost centres: three synthetic books, the third captured in a separate sitting whose own status read recorded TallyPrime 7.1, licence Silver, Education mode off; cost categories: two): the type-level numbering_method it carries is not the voucher type's numbering method: it read `None` for types a person had set to Automatic and to Manual on the screen, and the method is kept per number series, which `series_numbering` returns instead, so no value of numbering_method (`default`, `automatic`, `manual` or any other) says how a post is numbered. `series_numbering` was measured on one synthetic book (TallyPrime 7.1 Silver, Windows): 24 voucher types, each with one series named `Default`, of which three (Journal Automatic, Payment Manual with duplicates prevented, Receipt Manual with duplicates not prevented) were checked against Tally's screen; Automatic (Manual Override) through this tool (it is mapped from the series text measured on a synthetic book on 13 October 2026), more than one series, Multi-user Auto, a single series not named `Default`, a voucher type created new and other releases were not measured, an `unrecognised` method is never `manual`, and the integrated read, the two requests sent as one tool call, was run live on two synthetic books on 14 October 2026 and returned the numbering set or checked on Tally's screen for six types. `sub_method` is the series' own NUMBERINGSUBMETHOD (`auto_retain` is the screen's Retain Original Voucher No., `auto_renumber` its Renumber Vouchers, `absent` a series that printed none, and any other text, a blank one included, is returned raw under `unrecognised`); a Manual series printed Auto Retain too, which is not the numbering in force there, so it is not returned for one. It was measured on a second synthetic book (TallyPrime 7.1 Silver, Windows) and one voucher type, Receipt, set to Renumber Vouchers and back: with it on Renumber Vouchers, numbers already in the book changed, at the switch, when a voucher with an earlier date was entered by hand, and when one was sent by import without a number (the import's answer reported nothing altered and no voucher's AlterID moved); any other wording, a series that prints no sub-method, other voucher types, a batch of several vouchers, Gold, other releases and the same through ComplyEaze Bridge's own post are not measured. A value other than Automatic, Manual or Default is returned raw under `unrecognised`, not refused. `default` is Tally's reported value, not evidence that a type numbers automatically. The company's voucher-type count (NUMVOUCHERTYPES) did not equal the rows returned on two books (35 vs 26, 33 vs 24), and on one book equalled the number-series count (inferred to count series, unmeasured), so do not check these rows against it. The completeness of the voucher-type list is unverified: absence from it is not evidence that a voucher type is absent from the book. Under mask_parties, godown, stock-group, stock-item, cost-centre and cost-category names, their parents and a cost centre's category are masked, because a job-work godown, a supplier-named stock group or stock item or a customer-named cost centre can carry a party's name (Tally's reserved root as a parent is shown as ` Primary` and is not masked); a stock item's HSN codes and rates are not names and are returned as sent, but an HSN description, which Tally fills from its tariff list and a person can edit, is masked like an item name. Voucher-type, unit and account-group names are not masked: they are configuration labels, not counterparties. Education mode is refused. A first page (offset 0) always captures a fresh read and holds it in memory; a later page for the same kind (offset > 0) is served from it while the company's book extent, including ALTVCHID and ALTMSTID, is unchanged, at the cost of one small extent read. Each result reports `snapshot` (`id`, `master_alter_id`, `voucher_alter_id`, `read_at`, `reused`). Pass the first page's `snapshot_id` on later pages to have the call refused with `listing_snapshot_changed` (cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`) instead of continuing from a different read. A change that moves neither mark is not seen, so a later page can be up to 10 minutes old after such a change. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: Answer what is outstanding: receivable and payable totals from Tally's own paired bills reports, ageing, the top parties and the open bills, on a freshly observed supported product and mode and a date valid for the operation. `as_of` is optional: left out, it is this computer's date (`tally_status` `today`), and the date used is always returned as `result.as_of`, whatever the state. `open_bills_total` counts every open bill in the requested direction, all of which `totals` and the ageing cover, and `open_bills_shown` counts the bills on this page (`limit` is not lowered when the response size shortens the page): when shown is less than total, say so plainly, for example "showing 500 of 1,240 open bills; the totals and the ageing cover all 1,240" (on a later page, the bills from offset + 1; on a partial read, both counts and the sentence cover the base-currency ledgers only, so say so in it), and ask for the next bills with `offset` set to `next_offset`. `receivable` and `payable` follow the sign of each bill's balance, as Tally's own Bills Receivable and Bills Payable reports scope them, not the type of party: a customer's advance or a credit note raised to a customer appears under payable, and a supplier's advance or a debit note raised to a supplier under receivable, because those reports carry no bill type. That holds for an advance or a note kept as its own bill: an on-account advance goes to the unallocated figure instead, and a credit note set against an open invoice reduces that invoice. Measured on one synthetic book (TallyPrime Silver 7.1). Read a bill's `kind` as a direction, not as owed by a customer or owed to a supplier. An unallocated amount's direction is the sign of the party's net unallocated balance, so an on-account receipt and an on-account payment on one party net into one figure. A book with several Currency masters is read through the INR base Tally identifies. If it has ledgers kept in another currency (foreign_currency_ledgers_excluded, each with its currency) or base-currency ledgers whose balance Tally shows in another currency (base_currency_ledgers_mixed_excluded, each set aside with all its bills), the state is partial with partial_reason currency_ledgers_excluded and partial_reasons naming the lists that are not empty: figures cover its base-currency ledgers only, under base_currency_ledgers, never a total for the whole book, and both lists are always present, paged like the bills. Each unallocated party carries `ledger_bill_wise`, `opening_balance` (the ledger's opening as of the start of the books, with Tally's sign, so a debit opening is negative, never interpreted; absent when Tally sent none, which is unknown, not zero) and a `composition`: `not_bill_wise_ledger` (the ledger keeps no bills) or `bill_wise_ledger_components_not_separated` (what is left on a bill-wise ledger after its named bills: on-account entries, an unallocated opening, notes with no reference and anything else, not told apart). `amount` is a magnitude and `direction` says which side; `unallocated.totals.by_composition` splits the gross, receivable and payable apart, by those two over every party in the requested direction before paging (a row saved without one counts under `composition_not_observed`). No unallocated figure is labelled on-account. Party detail: with `party` (a ledger name) and `detail`, the result also carries a `detail` object for that party at the same as-of. The detail's `ledger_match` names the ledger read, how (`matched`: `exact`, or `case_or_spacing`, which the answer should mention by naming the ledger read) and any `similar_ledgers` that differ from it only in case or whitespace. Passing `detail` is the request to read the company's vouchers from the start of the books (or, for a named bill that Tally's bills reports list, from the earliest date they list for it) to `as_of`; nothing is read for a party detail without it. `bill_trail` (optionally one `reference`) lists every allocation of each bill in vouchers that are neither cancelled nor optional, oldest first, with state `tied` (the signed allocations equal Tally's own balance for that bill, or zero for a bill the report no longer lists), `trail_does_not_tie` (both numbers shown) or `bill_identity_ambiguous` (more than one native row or bill date for one reference, or a native row dated differently from the allocations; nothing is merged, and the native dates are shown). Naming a `reference` starts the read at the earliest date the reports list for it, so allocations dated earlier are not read, and a reference that carries two bill dates over the whole history, and is ambiguous there, can tie when named. The detail's own `state` is `bills_listed`, or for an empty list `not_bill_wise_ledger` or `no_named_bill_for_party` (no named bill in the vouchers or in Tally's list: a ledger that keeps no bills, one that is not a party's and a party with no bills are not told apart). The company's two change marks are read before the bills and again after the vouchers, and a detail whose marks moved is refused (`voucher_window_changed_during_read`); a change that moves neither mark is not seen (a letter-case-only rename of a ledger moved neither, in one book), and allocations that net to zero can still read `tied`. `unadjusted` lists the party's on-account, advance and pending note allocations and compares their on-account sum with the party's unallocated amount: `tied` means the two figures are equal, not that the composition is proven (components that net to zero are not seen); `residual_not_explained_by_vouchers` gives the difference and whether it equals the ledger's opening balance; `no_residual_row_for_party` (with `residual` null) means Tally lists no unallocated amount for the ledger (a zero residual, a ledger that is not a party's and a name that matched no row are not told apart), so nothing is tied; `not_bill_wise_ledger` lists no rows. Its rows are `row_amounts: as_allocated`: each amount is the allocation as made, never net of what later allocations adjusted against its reference, so an advance shows what was received, not what is left; what is still open on a reference is Tally's own `native_balance` beside the row, null when the reports do not list the reference or list it more than once (so no balance is chosen), told apart only by `native_rows`. Either detail is `window_returned_no_vouchers`, with nothing tied or listed, when the voucher read returned no voucher (that read is not corroborated). Cost and limits: the detail reads the whole company's vouchers (`window.company_vouchers_read`), costing a `vouchers` read over the same span, which is unmeasured on a large book, and any refusal of that read fails the whole `outstandings` call. Only when that read needs too many requests is the party read by its ledger alone (`window_scope` `ledger_scoped`, `window.party_vouchers_read`), and only for a ledger matched alone whose name its vouchers carry as stored, in single-spaced ASCII letters and digits with no operator word; otherwise the refusal stands and its `window_scope` says why. One foreign-currency composite voucher anywhere in the window fails it (`voucher_amount_invalid`, or `bill_allocation_amount_invalid` on an allocation). At most 128 data requests are sent (each sent twice, as every read is, with its census and the company marks besides), each holding at most 42 vouchers before anything is measured, so a window of more than 5,376 of the company's vouchers is refused unless the party is read by its ledger, and a smaller one may be. The refusals are `trail_window_too_large` (name a `reference` that `open_bills` lists for the party, and the read starts at that bill's date), `named_bill_window_too_large` (a reference was named already, so nothing narrows it further) and `unadjusted_window_too_large` (nothing narrows it, so it is not available for that party on that book), each with `reads.needed_at_least` against `reads.allowed`; a refusal comes before any data request when the count shows it, otherwise when a measured part does, with `window` listing any part already read. The detail needs a complete read (`detail_requires_a_complete_read`, with the read's own `partial_reason`) and refuses rather than cuts an answer of over 500 allocations: `trail_too_large` (name a `reference`) or `unadjusted_detail_too_large` (nothing narrows it). The limit counts allocations, not bills, so a party with very many opening bills can meet `agent_response_too_large` instead. For a ledger's master record (its group, opening balance and, with fields=compliance, GSTIN and party details), use ledger_masters instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

ageing_basis.description: Which date each open bill is aged from: due_date (the default) or bill_date. A bill whose date is after as_of has no age yet.

as_of.description: Optional: the day the open bills are read as of (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD). Left out, this computer's date, and the date used is returned as result.as_of.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

detail.description: Optional, with party: bill_trail (each bill's allocations) or unadjusted (the party's on-account, advance and pending note allocations). It reads the company's vouchers; the description gives its cost and limits.

direction.description: receivable, payable or both (the default). Direction follows the sign of each bill's balance, not the type of party.

limit.description: The most rows to return on this page. The default and the maximum are this server's row limit (500 unless it is configured otherwise).

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

party.description: Optional, for detail: a party ledger's name, spelled as in the book or differing only in ASCII case and spaces. A ledger whose own name differs in case or symbols from the spelling its vouchers carry is reached by either; `ledger_match` shows its own name and, when different, `ledger_row_spelling`, the spelling its vouchers carry. The bills are matched on the voucher spelling; what Tally's outstandings reports call such a ledger is not measured, so a detail that finds no bill for a party that has some is not proof it has none.

reference.description: Optional, with detail=bill_trail: one bill reference as open_bills lists it; the read then starts at the earliest date the reports list for that bill.

top.description: How many parties to rank by gross exposure (default 25). It ranks parties only; page the bills with offset and limit.

tools.description: Read a local SBI, HDFC, Union Bank of India or Bank of Baroda bank-statement PDF (password-protected; a statement that opens without a password needs password_file to be an empty file) and propose one Payment, Receipt or Contra per row (none for a cash line not yet answered), for build_import_xml's voucher shape. The whole run is refused unless the statement's account-number line ends with the digits in account_label (a Bank of Baroda number is masked: see account_label), and every row's running balance, the closing balance, and (where the statement prints them) the debit and credit totals reproduce the figures supplied exactly. A Union Bank statement, and a Bank of Baroda statement in the measured layout, print no opening or closing balance: take both balances from the books or the bank, since the statement cannot confirm them, and give an overdrawn (Dr) balance as a negative number (-16,141.16). tools.description: Read-only: a register of what the books record, not a GST return. It does not treat reverse-charge journals, imports (IGST paid at customs) or input service distribution specially: a voucher that touches a Duties & Taxes ledger is listed by the rule below and nothing more. A GST duty head does not say whether a ledger is input or output, and a Debit Note can be a purchase return or a debit note issued to a customer: each row carries `party_group` (the voucher party's predefined group, for example Sundry Creditors or Sundry Debtors, when it resolves) and the tool does not guess which it is. It inherits the compliance read's refusals (an INR base currency is required; a book too large to list is refused; see `ledger_masters`) and refuses with `register_master_mark_unavailable` when Tally does not report the master-alteration mark. Each page re-reads the masters and the window, so rows can shift between pages. Return the Purchase and Debit Note vouchers of a date window that touch a ledger under Duties & Taxes, with the tax each entry carries taken only from the GST duty head recorded on that ledger's master -- never from a ledger name and never from an amount. Reads the full voucher window before pagination (use narrow dates) and the ledger masters twice, before and after it. Per row: `tax_in_books` lists each entry on a ledger whose head ComplyEaze Bridge recognises as {ledger, head, raw_head, amount} (each entry also carries what the vouchers read carries on it, among it `cost_centre_allocations`, whose cost-centre and category names are masked as `vouchers` masks them); `duties_taxes_entries_without_gst_head` lists entries on Duties & Taxes ledgers that carry no GST head and never assigns them one: `observation` `not_tax_ledger` is a ledger whose own tax type is not GST (usually TDS or another payable), `absent` is a ledger with no head whose tax type is GST or was not reported, which may be a GST ledger whose head is missing (`tax_type` says which); `duties_taxes_entries_with_unrecognised_head` lists entries whose head is not in the recognised vocabulary or contradicts the ledger's tax type, with the raw spelling and its observation; `entries_on_ledgers_with_unresolved_group` lists entries on ledgers whose group chain could not be resolved; `taxable_entries` are entries on Purchase Accounts ledgers only (a GST purchase booked to a fixed-asset or expense ledger has `has_taxable_entry` false); `party_entries` are the voucher party's own; `other_entries` is everything else (round-off included) with no role inferred. `status` is the first that applies of head_conflict, has_unrecognised_head, has_unresolved_group, has_entries_without_gst_head, has_other_entries, complete. The response `state` follows the rule `vouchers` uses: `complete` only when every voucher read was checked against a separate count of the window (a census, which ComplyEaze Bridge sends for every book that has held a voucher, however few), otherwise `partial` with `reason` `nonempty_window_unqualified` and the rows still returned; an empty window is `complete` when its corroboration read confirms it. A row's `status` is separate: it says whether every entry the voucher touches classified, and the `state` does not change it. Amounts are as the books state them (negative is a debit), never re-signed and never summed across heads; there is no input-credit or direction field. `reference`, `party_gstin`, `is_invoice`, `post_dated` follow `vouchers`: absent means not observed, and `cancelled`, `optional` and `post_dated` vouchers are returned flagged, not excluded. Every other voucher type that touches Duties & Taxes (Sales, Journal, Payment and so on) is listed apart in `other_voucher_types_touching_duties_taxes`, not in `items`: whether it belongs in a return is the CA's call. A voucher with no resolved class is listed under `unclassified_voucher_type`; a voucher that touches only unplaceable ledgers under `vouchers_with_unplaced_ledgers`; a Purchase or Debit Note voucher with no entry on a Duties & Taxes ledger under `purchase_vouchers_without_duties_taxes_entry` (exempt or unregistered purchases, tax booked to a ledger filed elsewhere, or a cancelled voucher). A cancelled voucher is listed there with `cancelled` true whether or not it was taxed, because the cancelled vouchers measured came back from Tally with no ledger entries; a cancelled voucher that keeps its entries is not measured. Rows are in `items` (paged by offset and limit like `vouchers`); each has `has_taxable_entry`, false when no entry sits on a Purchase Accounts ledger (an item invoice may hold it in an inventory allocation). The side lists carry exact counts (`total`) and at most 100 items (`listed`); every ledger name in the response is masked like `vouchers` masks it. A voucher that names a ledger the masters do not list, a master or voucher that changed while the window was read, or a ledger set aside for its currency, refuses (`ledger_snapshot_drifted`, `voucher_window_changed_during_read`, `register_ledger_currency_excluded`) and releases no rows; a row dated outside the window refuses as `window_not_honoured`, or as `voucher_window_part_not_admitted` when the window was counted. A `sgst_utgst` head is a state-side head that a consumer summing state tax must include alongside `state_tax`. Not measured: a REFERENCEDATE on a sale, item invoices whose purchase ledger sits in an inventory allocation, and books with several currencies. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.
