tools.description: Tie the bank ledger in Tally to the bank statement already parsed by parse_bank_statement, at the start and at the end of the statement's own dates, or of the whole calendar months it was parsed for. Read-only: it writes nothing to Tally and never posts. Its check of the import journal takes the shared import-admission lock for a moment, so a build or post at the same time can be refused as lock-busy, and it can be refused by theirs; call again. It reads the proposals file named by proposals_id and proposals_sha256 (as build_import_xml does) and the book's ledger list three times: at the window's first date, at the day after its last date, and at the first date again, which catches a change dated before the window or an edit to the ledger itself (its opening balance, name or removal) made during the read (a voucher dated inside the window and posted during the read moves only the end figure and is not caught). No ledger is read when the file alone answers (window_not_recorded, window_narrower_than_statement, window_not_whole_calendar_months, window_beyond_statement_rows) or the window starts before the company's books begin (window_precedes_books_from). It reads no vouchers, and each ledger-list read has the same deadline and size limits as ledger_movement's. The proposals file is not bound to a company: pass the company_guid of the company the statement belongs to, because a different company that has a ledger of the same name is read just as readily. The window is the whole statement, from its first to its last row date, at the balances you supplied. A file parsed with from or to that left rows out is compared over those dates only if they are whole calendar months (from the 1st to a month's last day) within the statement's rows; the opening and closing are then worked out from the statement's own rows, so a gap together with the book's figure gives the statement's balance at the month edge. Any other window is not_established: window_not_whole_calendar_months, or window_beyond_statement_rows when a month starts before the statement's first row or ends after its last. So is a narrowed file written before parse_bank_statement recorded a window's balances (window_narrower_than_statement), and one written before it recorded the statement's dates (window_not_recorded); parse the statement again. The result carries the stage, the two dates, rows_without_voucher, three figures, a fixed reading and the company block. opening_gap is the book at the start of the window's first date less the statement's balance then; closing_gap is the book at the end of its last date less the statement's balance then, where stage before_build adds what this file's vouchers would put into the bank ledger (where the book would stand once the file is imported) and stage after_post is the book as it stands now; change_in_window is closing_gap less opening_gap. All three are in the statement's sign: positive means the book shows more money in the bank than the statement does. The book's own balances are not returned, but a gap plus the statement's balance at that date (for the whole statement, the balance you supplied) gives the book's balance, so they are derivable from the result. For whole calendar months the reverse also holds: the book's figure less a gap gives the statement's balance at the month edge, and change_in_window with the book's movement gives the statement's net over those months. These are totals per calendar month, never a part of a month except the part-months at the statement's own start and end, whose net a month edge's balance gives together with the opening and closing you supplied; but a month in which every other row's amount is already known (one row alone, or one row beside open cash lines, whose amounts parse_bank_statement returns) gives that row's amount. Each figure has a state: tied (exactly zero), differs, or not_established with a reason (window_not_recorded, window_narrower_than_statement, window_not_whole_calendar_months, window_beyond_statement_rows, window_precedes_books_from, bank_ledger_not_in_book, book_changed_during_read; for before_build also rows_without_voucher, when some rows of the statement have no voucher in the file because a cash line is unanswered or a row is skipped, and file_already_partly_posted, when the import journal already holds a row of this file, either of which leaves closing_gap and change_in_window not established). A gap does not say why: uncleared cheques and deposits in transit, a missing entry, a repeated entry and the wrong bank ledger look alike here, and the reading says so and prescribes no remedy. It checks the bank ledger only; a wrong party or expense ledger is not caught. Use it after parse_bank_statement and before build_import_xml with stage before_build, and again with stage after_post after a post or an import by hand. Requires one observed INR currency master, as ledger_movement does. Not yet proved against a live book. tools.description: Return the stock summary: the closing stock value per stock item as of a date, with the total of those values checked against Tally's own Stock Summary, and whether inventory is integrated with the accounts. The top-level `state` is one of three. `value_total_matched`: the items are returned, and their closing values add up to the sum of the top-level lines of Tally's own Stock Summary; only that total was compared, so `value_total_matched` can stand beside `partial` true when some items have no closing value. `no_stock_items`: Tally's own stock item count is 0, the item list is empty and the Stock Summary is empty; `items` is an empty list. `not_established`: no item is returned (`items` is null), `reason` says why and `remediation` says what to do next: `tally_stock_summary_differs` (the report has a total the items do not add up to), `tally_stock_summary_shows_no_value` (the items carry a value and the report has no amount; an empty report is not told apart from one Tally did not render) or `stock_values_not_comparable` (nothing could be compared). Such a result carries `unchecked_comparison` in place of `tie_out`, for investigation only: neither side is a stock value or a total, the items' side adds only the closing values present, and the closing-value total of a matched read is the only thing this tool checks. A `not_established` result is not held for paging, and it replaces any earlier read of the same date. A closing quantity of an item under the root is returned only where Tally's own plain Stock Summary shows the same item by name with the same quantity, unit and amount (`closing.quantity.state` `agreed`, with `amount` and `unit`). That report has no line for an item inside a stock group, so its quantity is its own row's in the item list, not compared (`inside_stock_group`, with `item_list_amount` and `item_list_unit`; equal to Tally's expanded screen on the one book measured). Other items say why not (`none_sent`, `unread`, `parent_not_resolved` for a parent reading Primary without Tally's root marker or carrying a marker anywhere else, `report_has_no_line`, `report_name_not_unique`, `report_differs`); `totals.closing_quantity_unread_count` counts quantities that could not be read (a compound unit, or a unit with a space), which do not refuse the read. `checks` says per field what is `checked`, `checked_where_agreed` or `not_checked`: the closing-value total is checked; the closing quantity only where `agreed`; each value on its own, the names, parents and base units, and whether the date was honoured are not. `as_of` (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD) must be a month's last day, not before the book's start or after today; any other date is refused as `stock_summary_as_of_not_measured` before any request. Month ends inside the year were measured on TallyPrime 7.2; a voucher dated on the end date was counted on a 15 October read, not at a month end; the company's own year start is not read. The period runs from 1 April (or the book's start, if later) to `as_of`. Each item carries `name`, `guid`, `parent`, `base_unit` and `closing`; `closing` holds `value` exactly as Tally sends it, and `quantity` (a `state`, with `amount` and `unit` when `agreed`, `item_list_amount` and `item_list_unit` when `inside_stock_group`). Empty is not zero: an empty closing value is returned as null and counted in `totals.empty_closing_value_count`, and a value sent as 0.00 is a value. Signs are kept, as in the trial balance: a negative value is a debit, which is stock held, and Tally's own Stock Summary screen shows it as a positive value (measured on one synthetic company, licensed TallyPrime 7.1 Silver). `value_sum` adds the values with their signs, so stock held gives a negative sum, and `totals.value_sum_signs` is always `as_sent_negative_is_debit`; `value_sum` is written at the scale of the values it adds, and is null with `partial` true whenever any item's closing value is empty. The opening quantity and value are read but not returned, because their as-at date is unmeasured. `inventory` reports `integrated`, `inventory_on` and `batchwise` as yes, no or unknown (unknown does not refuse), and `basis` states what Tally reported (`ISINTEGRATED`); how the books use these values (as closing stock, or against a Stock-in-Hand ledger) is not measured. An item valued at zero or with no value adds nothing to either total, so only Tally's own stock item count vouches for it; that count followed the one delete measured (one synthetic company, one sample), which is not proof of a complete list (`checks.item_list_complete` is `not_checked`). `item_count_cross_check` reports `rows`, `tally_count` and `status`: items are returned only when the two are equal. Otherwise the read is refused as `stock_summary_item_count_differs` (both numbers under `counts`); a count Tally did not give refuses as `stock_summary_read_failed` with cause `stock_item_count_unavailable`, and a Stock Summary this Tally does not recognise with cause `stock_report_unknown`. `items` (1 to 50 GUIDs, each once) filters what is returned from the held read; a GUID not found is listed under `items_not_found`, not refused, and `totals`, `tie_out` and `item_count_cross_check` still cover the whole book. The inventory flags, the stock items and the Stock Summary are each read twice inside one company, mode and book-extent bracket, or the read is refused. A book whose inventory is off is refused as `stock_not_enabled`, Education mode is refused, and a company split by year, whose sibling companies share the GUID, is refused (`stock_summary_read_failed`, cause `company_flags_not_one_row`). Small books only: the items are read whole only when the master-alteration mark (it counts masters of every kind) times an assumed worst-case row fits 16,000,000 bytes, a mark of at most 874; a larger book is refused before any item request as `stock_summary_too_large`, with `size`, and retrying refuses again. Typical stock-heavy client books refuse today. A row count or response size past what was admitted refuses as `stock_summary_bound_premise_violated`, or `stock_summary_extent_changed` if the book moved. Limits: company totals only, with no godown or batch split and no rates. The row shape and the tie were measured on one synthetic book on one licensed TallyPrime 7.1 (the tie also once on a client book); other releases and books are not measured. An item's `name` and `parent` are masked under mask_parties, because stock names can carry a customer's or supplier's name (Tally's reserved root as a parent is shown as ` Primary` and is not masked); `guid` is not masked and is what `items` filters on. A first page (offset 0) always reads afresh and holds the read; a later page for the same date is served from it while the book extent, including ALTVCHID and ALTMSTID, is unchanged, and each result reports `snapshot`. Pass the first page's `snapshot_id` on later pages to have the call refused as `listing_snapshot_changed` instead of continuing from a different read (cause `book_changed_since_first_page`, or `snapshot_not_held` for an id not held). A change that moves neither mark is not seen, so a later page can be up to 10 minutes old after such a change. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

tools.description: Answer which of 1–500 proposed vouchers are already in the book. `presence` is present, possibly_present or absent, and only `present` names a book voucher. A nonempty window is read as `complete` only when its rows were checked voucher for voucher against a count ComplyEaze Bridge made of the window first, as `vouchers` labels it; ComplyEaze Bridge makes that count for every book that has held a voucher, however few, so a small book can read `complete` too. A nonempty window not counted is `partial` with reason `nonempty_window_unqualified`. An empty window is `complete` only when a read widened by a day on each side is also empty and the company has no vouchers (`company_has_no_vouchers`); it is otherwise `partial`, with `empty_uncorroborated` when the widened read is also empty but the company has vouchers, and `empty_window_wider_read_nonempty` when the widened read found rows on the neighbouring days, which cannot count the window. `present` and `possibly_present` never need a complete window and are produced either way, but `absent` means absent from the *whole* window and is only ever produced from one proven complete — a proposal that would otherwise be absent from a merely `partial` window instead comes back `possibly_present` with reason `window_not_proven_complete`. The conditional decision basis can use a voucher number on a voucher type you declare `manual` — unique on both sides, within an observed voucher type, and never onto a cancelled or optional voucher; or, for a voucher ComplyEaze Bridge wrote into a file a person imported by hand, the narration marker derived from the supplied `batch_id` and `bridge_txn_id` together. A native post (`post_import`) writes no marker, so this tool cannot identify its vouchers: one edited or re-dated in Tally can read `absent` here. Check a natively posted batch with verify_import, which finds its vouchers by the GUIDs its post created once its binding is made, before posting any of them again. It neither accepts nor reads client remote identifiers. Supplying only one narration identity component is an error. The marker reaches only the current writer identity scheme; older-scheme ComplyEaze Bridge writes stay unidentified rather than matched. Date, party and amount only ever produce candidates, with the rule that surfaced each and no ranking or score. A type declared `manual` is checked against the book's own numbering before the window is read (the company's master mark and the voucher-type numbering, 20 more requests): the call is refused, naming the types, when the book does not number a declared-manual type Manual with exactly one series that prevents duplicate numbers, when the book holds no type of that exact name, or when the numbering cannot be read (Education mode included); otherwise the result carries what the book said as `numbering_read`, or only its counts (`types_omitted`) when the rows would not fit a share of the response budget. Every type declared manual is checked, whether or not a proposal names it. The check reads the book's numbering as it is now and holds for the moment of the read: it does not know how existing vouchers were numbered when they were entered, and a voucher type saved after the read is not seen. A call that declares no type manual reads no numbering and says so. Every voucher type a proposal names needs a declared numbering method; under `automatic` Tally discards the supplied number, so nothing can be decided from it. `absent` means absent from this window, so cover the dates the book could hold. A proposal comes back `absent` only when the window is proven complete, nothing in it resembles the proposal, a voucher type declared `manual` carries its voucher number, and the party was supplied and could be compared completely; a proposal with no party (a Journal has none), no manual number, or a party whose comparison was cut short comes back `possibly_present` with a reason such as `party_not_supplied`, `manual_number_not_supplied` or `party_not_decidable`, however complete the window is. Reads the full window before comparing; dense windows can fail source limits. Party names bind through the same rules as validate_masters. A reported difference on a `present` voucher is a finding for a person, not a work item: correcting a voucher by Alter or Cancel silently creates a duplicate instead (§9.7), and no ComplyEaze Bridge path can correct a voucher it did not write. This never dispatches import XML to Tally. To list the vouchers of a date window, use vouchers instead. Under automatic, Tally discards a supplied number, so nothing is decided from it. A type declared manual is checked against the book's own numbering before the window is read, and the call is refused if the book holds no type of that exact name numbered Manual with exactly one series that prevents duplicate numbers, or its numbering cannot be read.

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

to.description: The last day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

vouchers.description: 1 to 500 proposed vouchers to look for in the book; the description says what decides present, possibly_present and absent.

tools.description: Say, before a call, the most census reads one call of `vouchers`, `ledger_movement` or `verify_import` will send on this company (a read can be refused before its census ends), and the least time a call that is not refused earlier spends on the gaps between them. The census follows the company's voucher mark, not the window: this figure is for one call, a narrower window does not lower it, and reading N days in N calls pays it N times. It is as of this call's own read of the mark; the next call reads the mark again. It reads the company's identity and then its marks (one paired read with an identity check on either side), the opening every windowed call makes, and sends no census and no voucher request. The count and the floor are derived from the mark and the gate's rules, not measured on this book, and the floor leaves out every data part. No estimate is made: `measured` is constant text, whole calls recorded in the protocol reference with their census reads, data parts, host, date and confidence, each marked as not a bound. Nothing is refused on this figure; the one refusal it can state is the one the read itself makes (`voucher_window_book_too_large`). Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

tools.description: Return literal-window voucher evidence with curated metadata and redaction. Reads the full source window before selectors and output pagination; limit does not reduce Tally work. A `complete` window is held in memory for its later pages: a page after the first (`offset` above 0) is served from that read, with one marks read instead of the whole window, while the company's two marks (vouchers and masters) are unchanged, and its result carries `snapshot` (`id`, `master_alter_id`, `voucher_alter_id`, `read_at`, `reused`); `voucher_alter_id` is null when Tally's answer carried no voucher mark (a company that has never held a voucher), and a number, 0 included, is the mark Tally sent. `listing_snapshot_changed` has cause `book_changed_since_first_page` or `snapshot_not_held`; without `snapshot_id`, a later page whose window is no longer held or whose book moved reads the window again, and rows can shift between pages. A `partial` window is not held. A later page is served only for the same question: the same dates (a date is the same however it is written), the same voucher-type selector, search and grouping, and the `ledger` argument exactly as typed on the first page (a differently spelled `ledger` is a different question and reads the whole window again). Without `snapshot_id`, a page whose held window found the book moved reads afresh and carries `earlier_snapshot` (`offsets_do_not_continue` true): start again from offset 0. Only a page whose `snapshot.reused` is true continues the earlier pages: a later page with `reused` false or no `snapshot` is a fresh read whose offsets may not continue them. A change that moves neither mark is not seen; not established: whether a company feature or configuration change that alters export content moves a mark, whether a restored copy of the company with the same marks is told apart, and whether a remote writer's save shows in the marks at once. So a held page can be up to ten minutes old after its read finished; a first page is always read fresh. Use narrow dates; dense windows are unqualified and can fail source limits. `state` is `complete` only when the window's rows were checked voucher for voucher against a count ComplyEaze Bridge made of the window first, or the window was empty, a read widened by a day on each side was also empty, and the company has no vouchers (`reason` `company_has_no_vouchers`); otherwise it is `partial`, with `reason` `nonempty_window_unqualified` when rows were not counted, `empty_uncorroborated` when an empty window's widened read is also empty but the company has vouchers, and `empty_window_wider_read_nonempty` when the widened read found rows on the neighbouring days (the window's own read found nothing and those rows cannot count it, so an empty window beside a busy day cannot reach `complete` today). ComplyEaze Bridge makes that count for every book that has held a voucher, however few, so `nonempty_window_unqualified` is expected only when the company's mark reads zero while the window holds rows. Selectors and the search apply after the window is labelled, so a zero from a `complete` window is a checked zero. A voucher created, altered or deleted between the count and the read refuses with `voucher_window_part_not_admitted`, cause `part_census_mismatch`; call again. Each item carries `cancelled` and `optional` (always booleans; a source that omits or cannot assert either fails the whole read rather than guess). `post_dated` behaves differently: Tally asserts it on every voucher when the fetch list asks for it, and the key is left out only when a source does not report it (one old capture did, taken before the tag was asked for), so it is boolean only when Tally asserted Yes/No and is absent from the item when Tally did not report it. Absent is not evidence of `false` — it means ‘Tally did not say’, not ‘Tally said no’, and a caller must branch on key presence, not on falsiness, before treating a voucher as not post-dated. Neither this tool's listing nor `voucher_presence` filters out post-dated (or optional/cancelled) vouchers; the caller decides what a non-posting or unobserved status means for its own computation. (A `summarise_by` call is the exception: it sets aside cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers and counts them, and sums post-dated ones with a count.) `reference`, `is_invoice` and `party_gstin` follow the same absent-means-not-observed convention as `post_dated`: each key is present only when Tally reported a non-empty value for it, and its absence must not be read as false or as an empty string. `is_invoice` is a boolean exactly like `post_dated`; `reference` and `party_gstin` are non-empty strings when present. A captured book with no GSTIN recorded against a party's ledger has shown `party_gstin` absent on every voucher for that party, which is not evidence Tally cannot report one. Of the voucher-type selectors (at most one of `voucher_class`, `voucher_type_guid` and `voucher_type`), `voucher_class` matches by Tally's own class functions and `voucher_type` ignores ASCII case as Tally does. Voucher-type names are editable in Tally, so a display name that is a class name, or the reserved name of any type in scope, is refused as `voucher_type_ambiguous` whenever the types of that name are not exactly the types of that class or reserving that name; the types involved are listed in `candidates` (bounded to a quarter of the response budget, with `candidates_total` and `candidates_truncated`). Use `voucher_class` or `voucher_type_guid` instead. That check sees only the vouchers in scope: the window read, after any `ledger` filter. A type with no voucher in scope is not seen, and when nothing is in scope nothing is ambiguous. When a `voucher_type` name selects no voucher, one more read lists the book's voucher types: a name no type carries is refused as `unknown_voucher_type`, with the name as `requested` and every type in `candidates`, nearest name first (bounded as above); a name some type carries keeps its zero. A filtered result carries `voucher_types`: the types `included` and every type `in_scope` (name, GUID, own reserved name, class and row count), and each item carries `voucher_type_guid`, `voucher_type_reserved_name` and `voucher_class` (null outside the measured classes). A row whose type Tally cannot resolve, or whose class answers contradict each other or its reserved name, refuses the whole read. A voucher whose amount Tally stored as a foreign-currency composite (`-$ 100.00 @ I₹ 86/$  = -I₹ 8600.00`) is withheld, not read: it still passes every date, ledger and type check, and is then listed in `withheld_vouchers` (GUID, date, type, number and cause `foreign_currency_amount_unparsed`, up to 100) with an exact `withheld_total`, the same on every page. `items` and `total` then exclude it, `state` is `partial` with `reason` `vouchers_withheld`, and `coverage` says so; the `voucher_types` row counts still include it, and the listing is also bounded to a quarter of the response budget. Any other amount Tally did not return as a plain decimal still refuses the whole read, as does a composite whose foreign and base amounts differ in sign while the foreign amount is not zero. `ledger_match` names the ledger read, how (`matched`: `exact`, or `case_or_spacing`, which the answer should mention by naming the ledger read) and any `similar_ledgers` that differ from it only in case or whitespace. Search: `voucher_number`, `reference`, `narration_contains` and `amount` (a plain unsigned decimal, matched against the absolute value of any ledger entry of a voucher, so it finds an invoice total and a tax line alike) keep only the vouchers that satisfy every criterion given. With a search, each item carries `matched` (which criteria held and, for an amount, the positions in `amounts` that equalled it). A blank, over-long or invalid criterion is refused (`search_criterion_empty`, `search_criterion_too_long`, `search_narration_too_short`, `search_amount_invalid`), and a narration phrase is refused as `search_narration_redacted` where narrations are withheld from the assistant. A voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount is never dropped by an `amount` search, since its amounts cannot be compared: it stays in `withheld_vouchers` and the result stays `partial`. A held window is reused only for the same search, and only for the same listing or summary: a listing and a summary of one question hold separate windows. `voucher_types` counts are taken before the search, so with a search they do not add up to `total`. Summaries (`summarise_by`): Each bucket has `group` (a ledger name, a `YYYY-MM` month, a voucher type name, a group name or a cost centre), `vouchers` (an exact count, each voucher once), `debit` (zero or negative, as `ledger_movement` reports it), `credit`, `net` (debit plus credit) and `voucher_refs` (up to 5 vouchers by date, type, number and GUID; `voucher_refs_complete` says whether that is all of them; a `vouchers` listing without `summarise_by`, narrowed with the existing selectors, lists the rest). Debit and credit follow each entry's sign (a zero amount stays on the side Tally flagged it). A ledger bucket adds the entries on that ledger of the vouchers the window, selectors and search selected: with a `ledger`, type or search given, a counter-ledger's bucket holds only its entries on those vouchers, not that ledger's whole movement. A month or type bucket adds all the entries of its vouchers (debits and credits then equal in size), or only the selected ledger's entries when `ledger` is given. `entries_counted` says which: `all_entries` or `selected_ledger`. A `group` or `primary_group` bucket adds the entries of the ledgers under that group (every entry of the selected vouchers, also when `ledger` is given). A `group` bucket holds only the ledgers directly under that group, as the ledger master shows it (a ledger directly under the root is under `Primary`, with `reserved_name` null), so a predefined group whose ledgers sit in sub-groups has no bucket or a small one: its whole figure, descendants included, is in `subtree_totals` (each group on any bucket's chain with `covers`, `depth`, `vouchers`, `debit`, `credit` and `net` over everything under it, never to be added to a bucket of the same group, whose own `covers` says it holds only the ledgers directly under it, largest movement first, at most 60, with `subtree_totals_total` exact and `subtree_totals_complete`; they overlap, so they do not add up to `totals`). A `group` bucket carries `reserved_name` (empty for a group the book's user made), `chain` (every group from it up to the one under the root, nearest first, each with `name` and `reserved_name`) and `primary_group`. A `primary_group` bucket holds every ledger under the group directly under the root and is keyed by its reserved name, so a renamed predefined group stays one bucket and shows its current name in `group` (a group the book's user made there is keyed by its name). Each has `members` (the ledgers in it with their own `debit` and `credit`, largest movement first, at most 10), `members_total` (exact) and `members_complete`; a group bucket cannot be narrowed with a selector, so trace its vouchers through a member ledger with `ledger`. Group names are shown as the book has them (a group may be named after a party); member ledger names are masked when parties are masked. The groups are the book's masters read now, not the grouping in force on each voucher's date: each ledger's group chain is read before the window and again after it and must be the same, or the call refuses (`group_snapshot_drifted`, or `ledger_snapshot_drifted` if the set of ledgers changed). A ledger that the ledger list does not hold, or whose group chain cannot be walked, refuses the whole summary (`summary_group_unresolved`, with `cause` `no_parent`, `group_absent`, `group_name_repeated`, `reserved_name_missing`, `cycle`, `exhausted`, `top_group_not_under_root` or `ledger_not_in_catalogue`; `ledger` names the ledger that could not be placed, the group is not named, and `no_parent` also covers a parent group Tally returned that ComplyEaze Bridge will not carry). By construction a group summary adds 30 requests to the window read, with or without `ledger` (a paired, identity-bracketed read is 6 requests: the company's marks to size the ledger list first, then the ledger list and the group list before the window and again after it); in one live run each call took 64 requests (34 for the window and 30 for the group modes, as counted from the code); a book of thousands of ledgers was not measured: a book whose master-alteration mark is above 11,983 is refused first (`summary_group_book_too_large`; the limit is provisional and computed, not measured: 16 MiB, a size chosen here and not verified, over the compliance ledger read's estimate of 1,400 bytes a ledger, which that read measured at 1,104 (a book of 1,989 ledgers) and 1,221 (a real book of about 9,500) on its own list without balances, and this list read 1,175 bytes a ledger in one live run (51,698 bytes for a book of 44 ledgers; a small book, so the figure is not a basis to raise the limit); the mark is an upper bound on ledgers, so a smaller book may be refused, and the limit is about half of what the transport's own rule admits for the same list), a real book's group buckets may need several pages (use `offset`), and on a large book ledger totals are cheaper with `trial_balance`. Group summaries were checked once against a live TallyPrime 7.1 on one synthetic book of 67 vouchers: each bucket equalled the ledger buckets added up by the trial balance's own parent column and the call took 64 requests; a large book, a group renamed or moved while a window is read and a held later page were not run live. Each bucket has `position`, its place in the whole ordering (labels of ledgers can read alike when parties are masked, and a masked label cannot be passed back as `ledger`); to list a month bucket's rest, narrow `from` and `to` to that month. `totals` is the debit and credit the buckets add up to, `vouchers_summarised` the vouchers behind them, and `excluded_from_buckets` the cancelled, optional and entry-less vouchers left out (counted, not hidden). Post-dated vouchers are summed, not set aside: `post_dated_included` counts those Tally flagged Yes and `post_dated_flag_absent` those with no flag at all (the read asks for the flag and Tally asserts it on every voucher, so that is expected to be 0; only when it is not does a zero in the first prove nothing); a voucher type that does not post (a memorandum, a reversing journal, a sales or purchase order, a delivery or receipt note), if the book uses it and Tally exports it with ledger entries, is not told apart and is summed too: `basis` says so in the result. Checked once against a live TallyPrime 7.1 on a synthetic book of 67 vouchers (a year, 44 ledgers, a debug build of master at 4c30f3f9f): every ledger, month and voucher-type bucket equalled the sums over the listed vouchers, the 30 ledger buckets equalled `trial_balance` for the same year, each search returned what the same criterion selects from the listing, and a later page came from the held window in 10 small requests. Not covered: a memorandum, a reversing journal, a voucher withheld for a foreign-currency amount, `mask_parties`, withheld narrations, an item invoice with stock lines, paging of a summary past one page, `ledger` name resolution, another TallyPrime edition or release, Windows, a large book. Cost, from that one run: a plain read took 34 requests, about 7 s and about 6 MB from Tally; each ledger, month or voucher_type summary or search call reads the window again at the same cost, and `ledger` adds 12 requests there, four of them reads of the whole ledger list (a group summary adds 30 with or without `ledger`, below); for a month or more on a large book read ledger totals with `trial_balance` (it has no month or voucher-type grouping and no search; the same year's `trial_balance` took 34 requests and 2.5 s on that book; one day of vouchers took minutes on the largest book measured, a voucher mark of about a million). Bucket `debit`, `credit`, `net` and `totals` are plain decimals with trailing zeros dropped (`1000`, `-87900.5`); an item's `amounts` keep the two places Tally sent (`1000.00`). Withheld vouchers are not in any bucket and the result is `partial`. A voucher whose entries do not balance refuses the whole summary (`voucher_entries_unbalanced`). Buckets are ordered by the larger movement first (ledger, type, group, primary_group, cost_centre), ties in movement keeping the order in which the bucket was first counted in the window, or by month. A held window serves a later page of buckets as it serves a later page of vouchers. Each ledger entry's `bill_allocations` carries `reference`, `bill_type` and `amount`; where Tally sends them it also carries `bill_date` (YYYYMMDD, the original bill's date for an Agst Ref) and `credit_period` (a `value` and a `unit` of days, weeks or months, or `unit` `unrecognised` with its `text` when the text cannot be read); an allocation Tally sent neither for has neither. An entry's `cost_centre_allocations` lists its cost-centre rows as sent (`category`, `cost_centre`, `amount`); an entry without them has no such key (on an item invoice the goods line sits inside the sales or purchase ledger's entry: an allocation list beside it is read like any other, one inside the goods line is flagged as in a shape not recognised, and no captured item invoice carries allocations; category and cost-centre names are trimmed; the amount is as sent; both names are masked under `mask_parties`). The rows are not checked against the entry's amount. On the one book measured with two categories on one entry, each category's rows added up to the whole entry, so do not add rows across categories; `summarise_by: cost_centre` sums them per category and checks each category against its entry. An entry whose list cannot be read whole (a centre with no name or no amount, an amount that is not a decimal, a centre or a category named twice, a category with no name or no centre, a field sent twice, text that cannot be decoded, an empty allocation container, an allocation list in a shape not recognised) carries `cost_centre_allocations_unreadable` with a reason and no partial list, the rest of the response unchanged. A row's `party` is Tally's own PARTYLEDGERNAME for the voucher: on a Receipt, Payment or Contra it can name the bank or cash ledger (on TallyPrime 7.1 it did for a Receipt, a Payment and a Contra that ComplyEaze Bridge imported), so read the counterparty from `amounts`, not from `party`. With `bank_allocations: true` an entry that has a bank allocation carries `bank_allocations` (at most eight; each field a `state` of `absent`, `empty` or `value`, the value trimmed), or `bank_allocations_unreadable` with a reason; an empty `bank_date` is not a sign the entry is unreconciled, and the `reference` search does not look there. A transfer reference typed into a Contra's bank allocation sits in its `instrument_number` on both entries, not in the narration. An entry without it has no such key, which does not mean it has no allocation; one that cannot be read whole carries `bank_allocations_unreadable` with a reason. With `goods_lines: true` an entry of an invoice voucher that carries goods carries `goods_lines` (at most 1,000): each line's `stock_item`, and its `actual_quantity`, `billed_quantity`, `rate` and `amount` as a `state` of `absent`, `empty` or `value` (the value trimmed, a quantity or rate with its unit, such as `100.000 Kgs` or `25.00/Kgs`), with `batches` (at most 100: `godown`, `batch`, both quantities and `amount`) where Tally split the line; a Purchase line's amount is negative and a Sales line's positive, as the entry's. A line whose batch amounts do not add up to its amount, whose amount is not a decimal or that names no item leaves its entry carrying `goods_lines_unreadable` with a reason and no partial list, the rest of the response unchanged. Item, godown and batch names are masked under `mask_parties`. In the captures Tally sent goods lines under a ledger entry only on invoice vouchers, and the lines of any entry that carries them are shown: a Stock Journal showed none in the one read of it (TallyPrime 7.2, the answer is not committed); a Delivery Note, Receipt Note, Physical Stock and Manufacturing Journal are not captured, and an entry without the key may still have moved stock. Captured on Sales and Purchase invoices of two synthetic books (TallyPrime 7.1, one also on 7.2); not captured: a Credit or Debit Note with items, discounts, additional cost, a bill of materials, a foreign-currency line, a voucher typed on Tally's screen. To ask whether vouchers you mean to post are already in the book, use voucher_presence instead. Each call appends metadata-only receipt lines (tool, company, counts, request and response fingerprints; no book content) to ComplyEaze Bridge's local log on this computer; it writes nothing to Tally.

amount.description: Optional: an unsigned decimal such as 1180.50; only vouchers with a ledger entry of exactly this amount (debit or credit). Each item says which entries matched.

bank_allocations.description: Optional, default false: true adds each ledger entry's bank allocations (bank date, instrument number and date, transaction type, status), each field absent, empty or a value as Tally sent it. Nothing in them says whether an entry is reconciled.

company_guid.description: The company's company_guid, as list_companies returns it.

from.description: The first day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

goods_lines.description: Optional, default false: true adds each ledger entry's goods lines on an invoice voucher (stock item, actual and billed quantity, rate and amount, and each godown and batch row), the stock item as a name and each other field absent, empty or a value as Tally sent it; a quantity or rate keeps its unit. A Stock Journal showed none in the one read of it (TallyPrime 7.2, answer not committed); a Delivery Note or Receipt Note is not captured. The lines count toward the byte cap of the held page window (64 MiB).

ledger.description: Optional: only vouchers with an entry on this ledger, spelled as in the book or differing only in ASCII case and spaces. A ledger whose own name differs in case or symbols from the spelling its vouchers carry is reached by either; `ledger_match` shows its own name and, when different, `ledger_row_spelling`, the spelling its vouchers carry.

limit.description: The most rows to return on this page. The default and the maximum are this server's row limit (500 unless it is configured otherwise).

narration_contains.description: Optional: only vouchers whose narration contains this phrase (at least 3 characters), ignoring letter case, accent composition and runs of spaces. Refused where narrations are withheld from the assistant.

offset.description: How many rows to skip before this page: 0, the default, is the first page.

reference.description: Optional: only vouchers whose reference is exactly this, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. A voucher with no reference never matches.

snapshot_id.description: Optional, on a later page only: the first page's snapshot_id, so the call is refused (listing_snapshot_changed) rather than continuing from a different read.

summarise_by.description: Optional: ledger, month, voucher_type, group, primary_group or cost_centre. The result then holds buckets of debit, credit and voucher counts instead of the vouchers, over the same window, selectors and search; offset and limit page the buckets. group and primary_group sum each ledger under its group as the book has it now (see the description). cost_centre sums the entries' cost-centre allocations by category and centre; its result's `basis` says how they tie out.

suspense_tagged.description: Optional, true only, and only together with `ledger` (the suspense ledger): keep the vouchers on that ledger whose narration ends in a suspense tag ComplyEaze Bridge writes ("Bridge: purpose not confirmed; reclassify", or "UNIDENTIFIED - reallocate from" followed by the name of one of the voucher's own ledgers), allowing one trailing [BRIDGE:...] marker after it. Each item says which tag in `matched.suspense_tag`. This classifies by the narration text: it does not prove ComplyEaze Bridge wrote the voucher (the same text typed by hand matches), and a voucher on the ledger whose narration was edited after the tag is NOT listed, so also read the ledger without this filter and treat every voucher left over as still in suspense. Refused without `ledger` (search_suspense_tagged_needs_ledger) and where narrations are withheld from the assistant (search_narration_redacted).

to.description: The last day of the date range, included (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD).

voucher_class.description: Optional, at most one of voucher_class, voucher_type_guid and voucher_type: a reserved class, matched however the book has renamed its types, child types included.

voucher_number.description: Optional: only vouchers with exactly this voucher number, ignoring ASCII case and surrounding spaces. Numbers repeat across voucher types, so more than one voucher can match.

voucher_type.description: Optional, at most one of the three: one voucher type's display name, matched ignoring ASCII case. A name that could mean more than one class or type is refused (voucher_type_ambiguous).

voucher_type_guid.description: Optional, at most one of the three: exactly one voucher type, by its GUID. Another company's GUID is refused (voucher_type_guid_foreign).
